findings.practical_consequence: A planner cannot relocate every protected duty without deciding for itself which contract owns duties currently assigned to multiple layers; that can duplicate, omit, or preserve an unconditional subprocess despite the requirement that every obligation have one correct authority layer.
evidence: Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v3/requirements.json:FUT-004 requires every retained obligation to exist at one correct authority layer, and FUT-005 requires a complete replacement mapping without an unconditional scope-expanding subprocess.

Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v4/work/candidate-round-1.json:complete_replacement_mapping assigns whole duty sets to composite owners, including G8 to proposed G5/G6 plus research-plan-review methods, G19 to proposed G11 plus blocker-catalog, G22 to proposed G9 plus working-agreement, G23 to proposed G4/G5 plus blocker-catalog, and G24 to proposed G10 plus reproduce-first-verify.

Tasks/directive-system-vnext/research-v4/work/candidate-round-1.json:requirement_statuses[FUT-004].ownership_validation proves only that each duty ID occurs once in the mapping; it does not prove that each duty has exactly one owner. The research prose names broad stage ownership but does not allocate each composite row's individual duty IDs to one exact universal directive or downstream contract.
